question.text: Why is the scanning and uploading of DIS to the depository system important?

answer.text: It provides an audit trail and evidence in case of disputes about whether the client authorized the transfer
It speeds up the settlement process
It eliminates the need for OTP

explanation.text: The Logic: A Delivery Instruction Slip (DIS) is a paper authorisation signed by the client to debit securities from their demat account. DPs are required to scan/tag DIS images against the correct serial number within a short window (industry practice is two working days) and retain those images so that, if a transfer is later disputed, the depository can verify the signature and serial number on the actual instruction. That preserved image is the audit trail and the evidence pack used in dispute resolution. The Trap: Speeding up settlement is not the purpose — the DIS is already processed electronically once accepted; scanning happens after. Stamp duty is unaffected by scanning. OTP/2FA is a separate authentication for online instructions and is not eliminated by the DIS scan. Note: The cited NISM Series VI Depository Operations workbook pages explain the DIS, signature verification and the requirement that DPs scan/tag DIS images within two working days (with reports and penalties for non-upload), but the pages checked do not state in so many words that the rationale is "audit trail / dispute evidence". The framing above is general operational/regulatory knowledge of why depositories require the scan.
